newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco jails three Islamist students.
newsitem.headline: Morocco jails three Islamist students.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Tuesday sentenced three student followers of a banned Islamic movement to up to two years in jail for disturbing public order and violence against civil servants, the official MAP news agency said.
The Casablanca court sentenced Oussama al-Hayouni to two years in jail and his two colleagues Abdelfatah Kharbouch and Hassan Boukaffa to one year each, the agency said.
"Another group of 27 Moslem fundamentalist students, arrested by security forces last week, will appear on Wednesday before the tribunal for a similar charges," a Casablanca-based lawyer said.
"This group was apparently involved in what police described as demonstrations which disturbed the public order on the Casablanca university campus earlier this month," the lawyer said.
The students are followers of the outlawed Moroccan Moslem spiritual leader Sheikh Abdsalam Yassine, who is spending his seventh year under house arrest, police said.

Yassine's Al-Adl Wal Ihsane movement was founded as a charity in 1980 and applied for recognition as a political party a year later. The interior ministry rejected the request and it was banned in 1990.
Security forces were deployed around the court area and the university campus on Tuesday to halt demonstrations of support for the arrested students, the lawyer said.
